sections.title: Modern technology terms
sections.content:
Essential vocabulary for discussing technology:
• artificial intelligence (AI) — computer systems that simulate human thinking. AI is transforming industries from healthcare to finance.
• algorithm — a set of rules a computer follows. Social media algorithms decide what content you see.
• automation — using machines to do work previously done by people. Automation has increased factory productivity enormously.
• virtual reality (VR) — computer-generated simulation of a 3D environment. VR headsets allow users to experience immersive worlds.
• cloud computing — storing and accessing data via the internet. Most businesses now rely on cloud computing for data storage.

sections.title: Online behaviour
sections.content:
Words for how we interact with technology:
• digital footprint — the trail of data you leave online. Be careful — your digital footprint is permanent.
• cybersecurity — protection of computer systems from theft. Cybersecurity threats are increasing every year.
• screen time — time spent looking at electronic screens. Experts recommend limiting children's screen time.
• viral — spreading rapidly online. The video went viral overnight, reaching millions.
• obsolete — no longer in use, outdated. Smartphones made traditional cameras nearly obsolete.

sections.title: Tech impact on society
sections.content:
Discussing how technology shapes our world:
• disruptive — radically changing an industry. Electric vehicles are a disruptive technology in transport.
• surveillance — close observation, especially by authorities. City surveillance cameras raise privacy concerns.
• digital divide — the gap between those with and without tech access. The digital divide affects rural communities most.
• innovation — introducing new methods or ideas. Continuous innovation keeps companies competitive.

exercises.question: The data trail you leave when using the internet is your:
exercises.hint: Everything you do online leaves a trace.
exercises.explanation: Your digital footprint is the record of your online activity.

exercises.question: Technology that is no longer used because something better exists is:
exercises.hint: It's been replaced by newer technology.
exercises.explanation: Obsolete means no longer produced or used; out of date.

exercises.question: A technology that fundamentally changes an entire industry is called:
exercises.hint: It shakes up the existing way of doing things.
exercises.explanation: Disruptive technology significantly alters the way businesses or industries operate.

exercises.question: The gap between people who have access to technology and those who don't is the:
exercises.hint: It's about inequality in tech access.
exercises.explanation: The digital divide is the gulf between those who have access to technology and those who do not.

exercises.question: Protecting computer systems from hacking and data theft is:
exercises.explanation: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting systems and networks from digital attacks.

exercises.question: When content spreads rapidly across the internet, it goes:
exercises.hint: Millions of people share it quickly.
exercises.explanation: Content that goes viral spreads rapidly and widely across the internet.

exercises.question: Using machines instead of human workers to complete tasks is:
exercises.explanation: Automation is the use of technology to perform tasks with minimal human input.

exercises.question: The process of introducing new ideas or methods is:
exercises.explanation: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or products.
